messages:
carmen: Quick note-- saw p99 for /v1/generate jump in EU region after the deployment. p50/p95 unchanged.
monitoring-bot: alert: eu:/v1/generate p99 420ms -> 760ms at 13:04 UTC
trevor: same here. looks localized to eu-dedicated cluster. did we change batch tunables or kernel quantization there?
anya: we pushed a kernel tweak and raised batch_wait on eu-dedicated to favor throughput. also that cluster did not run the prefix prewarm.
sam: would expect throughput gains, but tail sensitive. curious why p95 unaffected. small sample of slow requests?
carmen: pulled sample_count for the window: ~0.4% of endpoint traffic hit that cluster; absolute samples ~60 in 10m.
trevor: smallish counts. recommendation: UI should mark percentiles with sample_count and a "stability" flag. if count < 100, show "low-sample: p99 may be noisy".
anya: agree. also add an overlay on endpoint panels to break p50/p95/p99 by deployment/pool so we can eyeball where tails come from without ad-hoc queries.
sam: practical ops steps: 1) rollback batch_wait to previous value on eu-dedicated 2) run prewarm for top prefixes 3) add a short-lived metric tag so dashboard can split by pool.
trevor: rollback started 13:12 UTC. prewarm kicked at 13:13 with `./prewarm --pool=eu-dedicated --keys=top100.txt`
monitoring-bot: incident stub created INC-2026-181 for eu p99 spike
carmen: after rollback p99 down to ~450ms at 13:18. prewarm still warming.
anya: follow-ups: CONS-534 (percentile sample_count + stability flag), CONS-535 (deployment-breakdown overlay), RUNBOOK-234 (deploy-health checklist: prewarm, batch parity, metric provenance). I'll file these.
sam: also think alerting should include sample_count and a suggestion line: "If sample_count < threshold consider low-confidence" to avoid pager churn.
trevor: good call. closing when stable for 30m. thanks folks.
